paper_title: Searching for Invisible Axion Dark Matter with an 18T Magnet Haloscope
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1 (KSVZ model reference values multiplied by stated factors)
notes: Paper reports exclusion limits as multiples of the KSVZ benchmark coupling |g_agamma^KSVZ|. The KSVZ reference value is approximately 3.92e-16 GeV^-1 (derived from standard axion model conventions). The three mass ranges with different sensitivities are: (1) 19.764–19.771 μeV at 1.5× KSVZ → g_agamma ≈ 5.88e-16 GeV^-1; (2) 19.772–19.863 μeV at 2.7× KSVZ → g_agamma ≈ 1.06e-15 GeV^-1; (3) 19.863–19.890 μeV at 1.7× KSVZ → g_agamma ≈ 6.66e-16 GeV^-1. Data points encode the mass ranges and corresponding coupling limits. The experiment uses an 18 T HTS magnet haloscope with a Josephson parametric converter, scanning 4.7789–4.8094 GHz. Local DM density ρ_a = 0.45 GeV/cm³ is explicitly stated in Eq. (1). No significant axion signal was detected; five candidate events from initial scan were ruled out by rescan. Systematic uncertainty on signal power is 9.5%. The extraction confidence is moderate (0.75) because the coupling values are reported relative to a theoretical benchmark rather than as absolute measured quantities, requiring conversion via the KSVZ model constant. | selector: text (sole candidate)
